source_text: Klagel. Jerem. 4, 22. Ἱκανὴν ἐξέτισας δίκην, ἐν ᾗ Ἐδὼμ διαδέξεται. τὸ δὲ οὐ προσθήσει τοῦ ἀποικίσαι σε ἢ πρὸς τὴν ἀνάκλησίν φησιν οὐ γὰρ ἐπιμενεῖς τῇ αἰχμαλωσίᾳ τὸ τέλειον μέτρον πληρώσασα· μειοῖ γὰρ τὴν δίκην ὁ θεός, οὐ προστίθησιν), ἤγουν εἰ πρὸς δευτέραν ὡς μὴ γενησομένην ἅλωσιν εἴρηται, πῶς ἡ μετ’ ἐκείνην ὑπὸ Ῥωμαίων ἐγένετο; μήποτε τοίνυν περὶ τῆς ἐσχάτης ὁ λόγος τῆς γεγονυίας διὰ Χριστόν, μεθ’ ἣν οὐ γέγονεν ἑτέρα. καὶ πᾶς Ἰσραὴλ σωθήσεται μετὰ τὸ πλήρωμα τῶν < τὴν ἀνομίαν ἀπολιπών· μεθ’ ὃ λοιπὸν ἡ συντέλεια, καὶ τῶν γηΐνων ἡ κόλασις, ἐκδεχομένης τῆς κρίσεως. ῥηθείη δ’ ἂν καὶ πρὸς τὴν ἐκκλησίαν ὁ λόγος, ἥτις ἐστὶ θυγάτηρ τῆς πάλαι συναγωγῆς «ἀμεταμέλητα γὰρ τὰ χαρίσματα τοῦ θεοῦ«, ἐξέλιπε δὲ ταύτης ἡ ἀνομία διὰ τοῦ θείου βαπτίσματος), ἣν οὐκέτι τοῖς ἐχθροῖς παραδίδωσιν ὁ φήσας· «ὧδε κατοικήσω, ὅτι ᾗρετισάμην αὐτήν« καὶ τὸ «ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ μεθ’ ὑμῶν εἰμι πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας ἕως τῆς συντελείας τοῦ αἰῶνος«, ὅτε καὶ τὴν ἀσέβειαν ἐστηλίτευσε τῶν φρονούντων τὰ γήϊνα.
pass_a_gloss: You have paid a sufficient penalty, in which Edom will succeed. And the “he will not add to relocate you” either speaks toward the recalling—for you will not remain upon the captivity, having filled the complete measure; for God lessens the penalty, he does not add—or if it has been said toward a second capture as not about to come to be, how did the one after that under Romans come to be? Perhaps, then, the word is about the last one that came to be because of Christ, after which another has not come to be. And all Israel will be saved after the fullness of the nations, having left the lawlessness; after which thereafter the completion, and the punishment of the gēïnē / earthly things, the judgment receiving. And the word would also be said toward the church, which is daughter of the synagogue of old (“for the gifts of God are without regret,” and her lawlessness failed through the divine baptism), which he no longer hands over to the enemies who said: “here I will dwell, because I chose her” and “behold I am with you all the days until the completion of the age”—when he also pilloried the impiety of those who mind the gēïnē / earthly things.
pass_b_english: You have paid a sufficient penalty, in which Edom will succeed. And the “he will not add to relocate you” (Psalm 132:14) either speaks toward the recalling—for you will not remain upon the captivity, having filled the complete measure; for God lessens the penalty, he does not add—or if it has been said toward a second capture as not about to come to be, how did the one after that under Romans come to be? Perhaps, then, the word is about the last one that came to be because of Christ, after which another has not come to be. And all Israel will be saved after the fullness of the nations, having left the lawlessness; after which thereafter the completion, and the punishment of the earthly things, the judgment receiving. And the word would also be said toward the church, which is daughter of the synagogue of old (“for the gifts of God are without regret,” (Lamentations 4:22) and her lawlessness failed through the divine baptism), which he no longer hands over to the enemies who said: “here I will dwell, because I chose her” (Romans 11:25–26) and “behold I am with you all the days until the completion of the age” (Romans 11:29)—when he also pilloried the impiety of those who mind the earthly things (Matthew 28:20).
